clue.text: A rally regularly held in old Asian city for capital street trader

indicators.note: something held in another thing sits inside it, so these letters go inside the city's name

parts.note: first part of Peking, the old Western name for Beijing
taken as written

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so only every other letter of rally is kept

parts.note: first, third and fifth letters of rally
rest of Peking, which wraps round the inserted letters

explanation.surface: A merchant from the capital goes to a rally held in an old Chinese city.
explanation.walkthrough: PEKING is the old name for Beijing, and A plus RLY sits inside it. A pearly king is a London costermonger whose clothes are covered in pearl buttons.
explanation.definitionFit: Pearly kings are traditional London barrow-boys or costermongers, so a market seller working the streets of Britain's capital.

clue.text: Eastern wharf maintaining a record for fairness in employment

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for Eastern

indicators.note: to maintain is to hold or keep, so the wharf word holds the record inside it

parts.note: a quay is a wharf where boats load and unload
A taken as written plus LP, a long-playing record

explanation.surface: A dockside on the east coast keeps a record of fair treatment for its workers.
explanation.walkthrough: An LP is a long-playing vinyl album, the standard crossword record.
explanation.definitionFit: Equal pay is the principle that men and women doing the same job receive the same wages, a matter of workplace justice.

clue.text: King put on upper-class, grand wig

parts.note: R is short for Rex, Latin for king
U is the crossword letter for upper-class
G is short for grand, a thousand pounds

explanation.surface: A monarch dons a grand, posh wig.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue the king's letter is put on top of the other two.
explanation.definitionFit: Rug is informal slang for a toupee or hairpiece, especially a poor one.

clue.text: Years working the borders of Kansas. Years and years

parts.note: Y is the abbreviation for years
a machine that is on is working

indicators.note: the borders of a word are its outermost letters, its first and last

parts.note: first and last letters of Kansas

explanation.surface: Someone has spent years labouring along the edges of Kansas, seemingly for ever.
explanation.definitionFit: Yonks is British slang for a very long time, as in 'I haven't seen her for yonks'.

clue.text: Popular elected government briefly upset with EU

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the word for government loses its tail

parts.note: a candidate who is elected is in

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and disturbed, so the letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: GOV is a short form of government, its ending dropped
taken as written

explanation.surface: A newly voted-in administration is shaken up by the European Union.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in vogue is fashionable at the moment, so widely liked and sought after.

clue.text: Former PM succeeded, with happy attitude all round

indicators.note: all round means surrounding on every side, so the other words wrap the letter for succeeded

parts.note: glad means happy
S is the abbreviation for succeeded in family trees
the tone of a remark is the attitude it conveys

explanation.surface: A one-time prime minister did well and had a cheerful outlook throughout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Former PM' is the definition; 'succeeded' looks like part of his story but supplies only the genealogical abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: William Gladstone was a Liberal Prime Minister of Britain four times in the Victorian era.

clue.text: This onion on reflection could make you cry

indicators.note: a reflection in a mirror is back to front, so the word is read the other way

parts.note: to blub is to cry, an informal word for weeping

explanation.surface: Thinking about it, this onion could bring tears to your eyes.
explanation.walkthrough: Onions really do make you cry, which hides that cry is the wordplay: BLUB read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A bulb is the rounded underground storage organ of a plant, and an onion is one such example.

clue.text: Express tribunal unfortunately admitting obstruction

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so the rearranged word takes the obstruction inside it
unfortunately suggests things have gone wrong, so the letters end up in a jumbled order

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
let is an old word for hindrance, as in 'without let or hindrance'

explanation.surface: A court sadly lets in an objection, it says plainly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Express' looks like a verb, but it is the definition: an express is a fast train. LET as obstruction survives in passports and in tennis.
explanation.definitionFit: A bullet train is a very fast passenger service, like Japan's Shinkansen, so an express.

clue.text: Filthy rich boy entertaining old English duke

indicators.note: a host entertaining a guest has them inside, so the boy holds the letter for old

parts.note: a lad is a boy
O is the abbreviation for old
E is the abbreviation for English
D is the abbreviation for duke

explanation.surface: A wealthy young man plays host to an aged English aristocrat.
explanation.walkthrough: O goes inside LAD, then E and D follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Loaded is slang for having lots of money, the same sense as extremely wealthy.

clue.text: Writer constrained by constant urge? Never!

indicators.note: something constrained by words is held within them, so the run of letters lies inside the following text

parts.note: the letters run across the end of constant, all of urge and the start of never

explanation.surface: An author says he is never driven by a constant compulsion.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivan Turgenev was a nineteenth-century Russian novelist, author of Fathers and Sons.

clue.text: Having one's head above water, beginning to accumulate cash in hand

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, which is all that is kept

parts.note: first letter of accumulate
a float is the ready cash kept in a till for giving change

explanation.surface: Someone just about solvent starts building up spare cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Afloat means both literally buoyant and figuratively solvent, keeping out of debt.

clue.text: Little green men fib during answer

indicators.note: during means in the middle of, so the fib sits inside the answer abbreviation

parts.note: ANS is the abbreviation for answer
a fib is a small lie

explanation.surface: Someone tells a white lie when asked about Martians.
explanation.definitionFit: Little green men is the joking stock image of creatures from outer space.

clue.text: Flexible group of musicians that might make a bundle

parts.note: elastic means stretchy, flexible
a band is a group of musicians

explanation.surface: A versatile pop group might make a fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: To make a bundle is slang for earning a lot of money, but here the definition means holding things together.
explanation.definitionFit: A rubber loop wrapped round letters or pencils gathers them into a tidy bunch.

clue.text: Measure of energy ultimately powering steamer at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused and all over the place, so the letters are scrambled
ultimately means in the end, so only the last letter of powering is kept

parts.note: last letter of powering
taken as written

explanation.surface: A gauge of the energy finally driving a ship out on the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: A gas meter records how much gas fuel a household has used, so it measures energy consumed.

clue.text: Maybe 20 spoilers? A tad naughty!

definitions.note: 20 is EPIC POEM, and this answer is one example

indicators.note: naughty means badly behaved, so the letters misbehave and fall out of order

parts.note: taken as written, every letter used

explanation.surface: Giving away the plot of a long poem is a little bit wicked.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on 20-across, EPIC POEM.
explanation.definitionFit: Milton's Paradise Lost is the best-known English epic, telling of the Fall in twelve books of blank verse.

clue.text: Play in which Puck comes to a sticky end?

definitions.text: Play in which Puck comes to a sticky end?

parts.words: Play in which Puck comes to a sticky end?
parts.note: surface reading: a staging of A Midsummer Night's Dream where Shakespeare's sprite meets a nasty fate

parts.words: Play in which Puck comes to a sticky end?
parts.note: setter's reading: a sport in which the puck is struck by the end of a stick

explanation.surface: A drama in which Shakespeare's mischievous fairy meets a grisly death.
explanation.walkthrough: Puck is a character in A Midsummer Night's Dream; with a small p it is the rubber disc hit in a winter sport.
explanation.definitionFit: Players on a rink use sticks to drive a hard rubber disc into the goal.

clue.text: Listen to intro from Hammond organ? Absolutely!

parts.note: to hear is to listen to

indicators.note: the intro of a word is its opening, so only its first letter is used

parts.note: first letter of Hammond
the ear is the organ of hearing

explanation.surface: Someone urges us to listen to the opening bars on a Hammond organ.
explanation.walkthrough: The Hammond is an electric organ, but organ here is the body part.
explanation.definitionFit: The cry used in Parliament and at meetings to express strong agreement with a speaker.

clue.text: An important character in the school play

definitions.text: An important character in the school
definitions.meaning: first meaning: the janitor who looks after the buildings

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a role in a school drama production; the two parts are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The school caretaker maintains the premises, and Pinter wrote a well-known stage work of that title.

clue.text: Commander barking mad, terrible liar

indicators.note: barking is British slang for crazy, so the letters go wild
terrible means very bad, so the letters come out badly ordered

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A crazed officer in charge is a dreadful fibber.
explanation.walkthrough: Barking, short for barking mad, is British slang for insane.
explanation.definitionFit: An admiral is a senior naval officer who commands a fleet.

clue.text: Front page headline about power cut

indicators.note: about means around, so the word for cut surrounds the power letter

parts.note: to slash is to cut
P is the symbol for power

explanation.surface: A newspaper's lead story concerns a blackout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Power cut' reads as a blackout, but power gives P and cut gives SLASH.
explanation.definitionFit: In journalism a splash is the main story given big display on a newspaper's cover.

clue.text: Kept nice spot semi uncovered always for magnum opus

indicators.note: uncovered means stripped of its outer layer, and always says every word is treated that way

parts.note: Kept without its outer letters
nice without its outer letters
spot without its outer letters
semi without its outer letters

explanation.surface: A pleasant spot and a semi-detached house are a writer's masterpiece.
explanation.walkthrough: A semi is British for a semi-detached house.
explanation.definitionFit: A long heroic narrative in verse is often regarded as a poet's greatest work.

clue.text: Sweet wine container always crossing river

parts.note: a can is a container

indicators.note: the word for always lies across the river letter, taking it inside

parts.note: ay is an old and poetic word for always
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A tin of dessert wine is always carried over the river.
explanation.walkthrough: AY (also spelt aye) means ever in old poetry.
explanation.definitionFit: Canary was a sweet fortified wine from the Canary Islands, popular in Shakespeare's day.

clue.text: Small part arrived, leading to Oscar

parts.note: came means arrived
Oscar is the NATO alphabet word for O

explanation.surface: A bit part in a film turns out to win an Academy Award.
explanation.walkthrough: Oscar tempts as the film award but is just O.
explanation.definitionFit: A cameo is a brief appearance by a famous actor in a film or play.

clue.text: Enquire after cross spun fabric

indicators.note: after places the enquiring word second, behind the turned-round word for cross
spun means turned round, so the word for cross faces the other way

parts.note: cross means angry, and so does mad
to enquire is to ask

explanation.surface: Someone asks about a woven material that has been made into yarn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Enquire after' looks like a single phrase meaning ask about someone's health, but it splits into two jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: Damask is a rich reversible woven material with a pattern, often silk or linen.

clue.text: A sheepish character papa, in his dotage, ran amok

parts.note: a ram is a male sheep
Papa is the NATO alphabet word for P
someone in his dotage is old and aged

explanation.surface: An embarrassed, elderly father went on a wild spree.
explanation.walkthrough: Sheepish suggests shy, but here it means belonging to sheep.
explanation.definitionFit: To rampage is to rush about violently and destructively, just like running wild.

clue.text: Maurice occasionally knocked out a French classic

indicators.note: knocking out letters now and then removes every other one, leaving the rest

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters of Maurice

explanation.surface: A man called Maurice now and again was beaten in a famous French contest.
explanation.walkthrough: The Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe is a major horse race run at Longchamp in Paris.
explanation.definitionFit: The Arc, as racing people call it, is one of the great classic flat races of France.

clue.text: Country hotel acquired by bad lot

indicators.note: something acquired by a person is taken into their possession, so it goes inside

parts.note: a cad is a dishonourable man, a bad lot
Hotel is the NATO alphabet word for H

explanation.surface: A rural inn is bought up by a scoundrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country hotel' reads as one phrase, but Country is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Chad is a landlocked nation in north-central Africa.

clue.text: Caution driver initially in pursuit of New York taxi?

parts.note: New York cabs are famously yellow cars

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so just the opening letter of driver is used

parts.note: first letter of driver

explanation.surface: A warning to a motorist chasing a New York cab.
explanation.walkthrough: In pursuit of puts the driver's D behind the yellow car.
explanation.definitionFit: In football a referee shows this to book a player, an official caution for misconduct.
